lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Breakbeat Observatory! Ninety four point eight! Drum and bass from the top of Mount Subwoofer!

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: This is Breakbeat Observatory. A hundred and seventy two beats a minute, at the speed of light. Hold on to your stars.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: MC Parallax, Breakbeat Observatory. Dome open, woofer up, and every star in the sky is shivering. Lovely.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Breakbeat Observatory. Clear skies, heavy bass, perfect seeing conditions. Let's see what we can hear.

lines.speaker: Doctor Ferrin
lines.text: Breakbeat Observatory. Twenty three forty. Bass detected.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: She's right, you know.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: You're locked to Breakbeat Observatory. Signal strength, massive. Distance, a few light years, give or take a drop.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Breakbeat Observatory! Big up every galaxy listening right now. All two trillion of you.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: That last tune was a hundred and seventy four beats a minute, and nine minutes long, which, at the speed of light, is about a hundred million miles.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: So if you're listening from the sun, it just got to you. Big up the sun! Here's the next one.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Shout-outs! Big up the Lesser Teacup Cluster. Big up the Velvet Spiral, all two hundred billion stars, I see you.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: And big up Gorbel's Nebula, who requested this one about thirty thousand years ago. Sorry for the wait, Gorbel. Worth it.

clips.title: An Apology to the Brantley System

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Quick apology to everybody in the Brantley System. That last drop moved your sun about four inches to the left. Your summers might be a bit warmer for a while. Our bad.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Here's something lighter.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: It's not lighter.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Up in the dome tonight, as always, it's Doctor Ferrin, our resident astronomer. Headphones on. Notebook out. Writing down every single drop.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Three hundred nights a year she's up there, and she has never once nodded her head. Not once. Doc, how are we doing?

lines.speaker: Doctor Ferrin
lines.text: Recording.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: That's the vibe.

lines.speaker: Doctor Ferrin
lines.text: Observation log. Twenty three fifty one. The drop. Twenty three fifty one and four seconds. A star in Cassius Minor has moved.

lines.speaker: Doctor Ferrin
lines.text: Twenty three fifty two. The star has moved back. It appears to be dancing. Noted.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Noted! She noted it! Here's another one!

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Breaking news from the dome. I think. I think I just saw Doctor Ferrin's foot tap. Once. Doc, did your foot just tap?

lines.speaker: Doctor Ferrin
lines.text: It was a calibration.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: It was a calibration, people! Calibrate with me!

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Okay. I need everybody to stay very calm. About thirty seconds into that last tune, Doctor Ferrin nodded her head. Once. Slowly.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: And then she wrote something down, and underlined it twice. I don't know what it says. I'm not going to ask. Some things you just let be beautiful.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: If you're listening from the Andra Reach, you're hearing this set sixty thousand years from now. Hello, the future! Is the party still going?

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: It is? I knew it! Tell them Parallax said hi. Here's one for the future.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Technical note. The main woofer got a new cone this week. The old one had been pointed at the sky so long it started picking stuff up. Last night it played us a bassline from a planet that hasn't been named yet.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: So we kept it. It's in the gift shop. It's still going.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Big, big shout to the Nightjar! Relay Seven! The night operator! I see your running lights. You're the closest listener we've got, about one point four light seconds out. Basically next door.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Turn it up. The neighbours won't mind. You haven't got any.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: The sun's coming up over Mount Subwoofer, which means we have to turn down. The sun is very loud. Five thousand degrees of pure treble. We can't compete.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: One more tune, then the dome closes. Make it count.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Picking something up on the big woofer. Very faint. A man called Teodor, at Relay Four, asking if anyone can hear him.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Teodor! We hear you, my friend! Here's one with extra sub, so it gets all the way out to you. Big up Relay Four!

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Evening, everybody! The sky's getting dark, which in our line of work means the speakers come out. The stars are tuning up. The moon's found a spot near the front.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: It's going to be a big one tonight.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Breakbeat Observatory, this is the Drop Zone! Dome open, woofers armed. Nearby planets, please secure any loose moons.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Seismic update! The Drop Zone just registered a four point two on the observatory floor, and a mild tremor in the next valley, where some goats are now facing the other way.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Sorry, goats. Here comes another one.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: If you're in the dome tonight, watch out for the meteor shower. Those aren't meteors. Those are the stars we shook loose earlier.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: They'll be fine. Probably. Doc?

lines.speaker: Doctor Ferrin
lines.text: Probably.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: It's late, and this is the Late Night Light Cone. Everything you hear tonight leaves here at the speed of light, and it's not slowing down.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: After midnight the bass travels further. Every tune we play tonight is going to be heard, eventually, by somebody very far away and very surprised.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Let's give them something to be surprised about.

lines.speaker: Doctor Ferrin
lines.text: Observation. Oh two hundred hours. It is very late. The music has not stopped.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: It's never stopping, Doc. Write that down.

lines.speaker: Doctor Ferrin
lines.text: Never... stopping. Noted.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: This is Closing the Dome, on Breakbeat Observatory. Last tunes before the sun comes up and drowns us out. Doc, final observations, please.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Doc's packing up her notebook. She's filled another one tonight. That's three thousand notebooks, people, every page full of drops.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: One day we're going to read them all out, start to finish. That'll be a long show.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: The sky's going pale. The stars are fading out, one by one, like a crowd going home.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Thank you, stars. Get home safe. See you tonight.

clips.title: A Ghost with a Sound System

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Halloween special, people! Tonight we pointed the woofer at a star that died a million years ago. It's still sending us its light. And, it turns out, its bass.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: That's a ghost, people. That's a ghost with a sound system. Doc?

lines.speaker: Doctor Ferrin
lines.text: Observation. Spooky.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: She's never written spooky before.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Breakbeat Observatory. Happy Halloween. Half the stars you can see are already gone. Dance anyway.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Moon Goes Missing

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: People, a moon's gone missing, and nobody can agree which one! Doc, did we move it? Did that last drop move a moon?

lines.speaker: Doctor Ferrin
lines.text: Checking. No. We moved two. Both accounted for.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Phew!

lines.speaker: Doctor Ferrin
lines.text: Observation. Toast.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: She's right! The whole dome smells like toast, and so does the rest of the multiverse! Big up whoever's on breakfast!

clips.title: The Convergence: The Song Nobody Can Finish

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Everybody's got the same tune stuck, people, and nobody can finish it! We pointed the telescope at the far end of the universe to see if they've got the ending. Doc?

lines.speaker: Doctor Ferrin
lines.text: Observation. They're also humming it.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Three knocks on the observatory door! Right on the beat! Doc went to look. Nobody.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Whoever you are, you're welcome at the front. Lovely timing.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Colour With No Name

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Whoa. The sky just did a colour. Doc, log it!

lines.speaker: Doctor Ferrin
lines.text: Observation. I don't have a word.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: She's never not had a word, people. That's historic.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: There's a pigeon in the dome, standing right next to Doctor Ferrin. And people, the pigeon's head is nodding.

lines.speaker: MC Parallax
lines.text: Doc? Doc's head is... no. Not yet. Close, though!
